question: Power integration: 5x^2 from 1 to 2 equals 35/3 units. A 55-kilogram mass at this value (as velocity in m/s) has kinetic energy. Convert to kilojoules, subtract 13, scale by 5, add 5. The load carrier capacity is 200 kg, not applicable. What is the energy in kJ?

A sequence sum: (2*1-1) + (2*2-1) + ... + (2*7-1) = 49. A 41-kilogram mass at 49 m/s has kinetic energy. Convert to kilojoules, scale by 7, then 5, add 15. The mass identifier is P-2024, irrelevant. What is the energy in J?

Acceleration: second derivative of 2x^3 - 4x^2 at x = 1. A 17-kilogram mass at this acceleration (in m/s²) has kinetic energy. Scale by 10, convert to kilojoules, scale by 3, add 22. The mass shape is cylindrical, not applicable. What is the energy in kJ?

A force control system operates at different settings. The base setting is 2 times the sum of 8 and 2, giving 20 units. A 37-kilogram mechanism operating at this setting (in m/s²) generates a reaction force. Scale by 9 for mechanical advantage, convert to kilojoules, add 19 kN for safety buffer, then scale by 10 for the complete array. The mechanism housing weighs 2.5 kilograms, which is not used. What is the final control force in kN?

A rotating shaft experiences variable torque. The torque rate follows 5x^3 + 2x^2 with first derivative at x = 1.0. A 64-kilogram rotor mass responds at this rate (in m/s²). Scale the force by 10, then by 4, add 4 kN, subtract 27 kN. The shaft diameter is 50 millimeters, not applicable. What is the final shaft torque in N?

A probabilistic system has 13 choose 2 = 78 possible states. The system operates at state 78 minus 24 = 54. With a 46-kilogram load at this state (as velocity in m/s), calculate kinetic energy. Scale by 6, convert to kilojoules, scale by 3. The system has 8 parallel channels, which doesn't factor in. What is the state energy in kJ?

A spring mechanism has parameters satisfying x^2 - 11x + 24 = 0; use the larger root. Multiply by 4, add 6 to get the effective spring constant. With a 3-kilogram mass at this constant (as acceleration in m/s²), calculate energy. Scale by 8 for oscillations. The spring material is stainless steel, not needed. What is the oscillation energy in J?

An acceleration profile has second derivative 4x^3 - 4x^2 at x = 3. A 52-kilogram mass responds with kinetic energy at this acceleration. Add 2 kJ, subtract 21 kJ, subtract 21 more kJ for baseline. The mass is mounted on a 0.5-meter bracket, not used. What is the final energy in kJ?

A mechanical factor system: gcd(279, 133) = 19. Multiply by 9 to get 171, add 23 to get 194. With a 20-kilogram mass at this velocity (in m/s), calculate kinetic energy. Scale by 2, convert to kilojoules. The supporting frame height is 3 meters, not applicable. What is the energy in kJ?

A drive system parameter satisfies x^2 - 8x + 15 = 0; select the larger root. A 187-kilogram motor operating at this rate (in m/s²) generates force. Convert to kilojoules, scale by 4, then by 9. The motor cool-down time is 30 minutes, not needed. What is the drive force in kN?

A transmission system factor: gcd(303, 264) = 3. Add 23 to get 26. A 150-kilogram transmission responds at 26 m/s² (force). Add 6 N, scale by 11, subtract 11. The gear ratio is 3.5:1, not used. What is the transmission force in N?

A system parameter satisfies x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0; pick the smaller root. A 32-kilogram load at this velocity (in m/s) has kinetic energy. Scale by 2, then by 10. The load container has 5-liter volume, not used. What is the total energy in kJ?

A constraint satisfies x^2 - 13x + 40 = 0; use the larger root. Add 14. A 95-kilogram mechanism at this value (in m/s²) generates force. Convert to kilojoules, subtract 26, subtract 5 more. The mechanism housing capacity is 200 liters, not relevant. What is the final force in kN?
Integration: 2x^2 + x from 0 to 4 equals 136. A 57-kilogram mass at 136 m/s has kinetic energy. Scale by 4, then 3, add 23. The mass location is lab-B, irrelevant. What is the energy in J?
A factor: gcd(322, 326) = 2. A 149-kilogram system at 2 m/s² generates force. Add 11, scale by 4 twice, add 24. The system model is 2024-X, not needed. What is the force in N?

Parameter x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0; pick larger root. A 21-kilogram load at this velocity (in m/s) has energy. Subtract 15, convert to kilojoules, subtract 18. The load material is aluminum, irrelevant. What is the energy in kJ?

Integration: x^2 + 2x from 2 to 3 equals 19/3. A 152-kilogram structure at this value (in m/s²) generates force. Subtract 4, add 9, scale by 9. The structure section is A-1, not needed. What is the force in N?

Parameter x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0; smaller root times 12 equals 12. A 154-kilogram system at 12 m/s² generates force. Convert to kilojoules, scale by 9. The system age is 5 years, not applicable. What is the force in kN?

Parameter x^2 - 15x + 56 = 0; smaller root plus 5 equals 13. A 154-kilogram mechanism at 13 m/s² generates force. Convert to kilojoules, scale by 12 then 9. The mechanism rating is 50 kW, not used. What is the force in kN?
Integration: 2x^2 from 3 to 4 equals 74/3. Add 25 to get ~99. A 21-kilogram mass at ~99 m/s has energy. Scale by 2 then 11. The mass shape is cubic, not applicable. What is the energy in J?

Integration: 3x^2 + 2x from 1 to 3 equals 44. Add 28. An 8-kilogram mechanism at 72 m/s² generates force. Convert to kilojoules, scale by 12. The mechanism housing is steel, irrelevant. What is the force in kN?

Integration: x^2 + 5x from 0 to 4 equals 112/3. A 37-kilogram load at this value (as velocity) has energy. Convert to kilojoules, add 23, scale by 8 then 4. Displacement: 12 meters, not needed. What is the energy in kJ?
Combinations: 8 choose 4 = 70. A 2-kilogram load at 70 m/s has energy. Subtract 25, add 25, add 6, convert to kilojoules. Diameter: 40 mm, not used. What is the energy in kJ?

Parameter x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0; larger root. A 107-kilogram mechanism at this acceleration generates force. Add 28, convert to kilojoules, subtract 14. Material: titanium, irrelevant. What is the force in kN?

Integration: 4x^2 + 4x from 1 to 3 equals 88. A 114-kilogram system at 88 m/s² generates force. Convert to kilojoules, subtract 22, scale by 9, subtract 11. Model code: S-442, not needed. What is the force in kN?
